newsitem.title: TURKEY: Business group calls for new Turkish government.
newsitem.headline: Business group calls for new Turkish government.

text.p: A leading Turkish business group on Monday called for a new government to cool down the country's overheated political temperature and find solutions to problems.
"Only new formations can reduce the voltage," Muharrem Kayhan, chairman of the business group TUSIAD, told reporters.

"A new (government) formation should be put into place, whether it be good or bad...We would prefer a government as broad-based as possible, and which would produce solutions to the country's problems," he said.
Turkey's ruling Islamist-conservative coalition has been under pressure from secularists, particularly to powerful army, since it was formed in June last year.
The government has recently been embroiled in a row with the army over Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's attempts to bring Islamist norms into public life.
Opposition parties and government discontents have called for a new alliance to replace Erbakan's coalition, but the fractious anti-government group has as yet failed to come up with an alternative.
TUSIAD's Kayhan said any alternative would have to be well thought out in order to implement necessary reforms in the political party law, the electoral law, social security and administrative areas.
